paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Jacob is dying, and he spends his last strength on promises. He makes Joseph swear to carry him out of Egypt and bury him with his fathers (Genesis 47:29-30). Then he sits up in bed and tells Joseph, "God will be with you and bring you back to the land of your fathers" (Genesis 48:21). I think this old man is looking past Egypt, past the bed, and straight at what God said He would do.

Now look at those crossed hands. Joseph moves to fix them, and Jacob says, "I know, my son, I know!" (Genesis 48:19). The younger boy gets the greater blessing, and nobody earned it. Manasseh did nothing wrong by being born first. God just doesn't hand out His blessings by lining us up in birth order. I've been the worn-out stamper at the back of a drawer, so believe me when I say that gives me HOPE.

Jacob also calls God "the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day" (Genesis 48:15). That's a man who looked back over a long, rough road and saw God leading him the whole way. So here's what I want you to take to your own counter, baker. Your place in God's plans doesn't depend on your rank, your résumé, or how clean your edges are. It rests on the God who shepherds, who keeps His promises, and who is still telling this family's story.
